name: Shahnameh
pronunciation: shah-nah-MEH, Persian for Book of Kings
about: Shahnameh comes from the wedding of Siyavush and Farangis. Deep violet and pavilion blue give the page its quiet center, while garden green, gold, parchment and red carry the celebration around it. I wanted the palette to hold both the stillness of the couple and the music outside their room.
story: The [Shahnameh](https://shahnameh.fitzmuseum.cam.ac.uk/literary), or Book of Kings, is Ferdowsi's great Persian epic. It gathers Iran's legendary and historical past into verse. Its lasting importance lies not only in the stories, but also in the way Ferdowsi strengthened Persian as a literary language and carried cultural memory across generations.

Siyavush is the son of the Iranian shah Kai Kavus. After trouble with his father drives him into exile in Turan, he marries Farangis, the daughter of Afrasiyab. Their son Kai Khusrau will later become shah of Iran. The miniature places the couple together inside a pavilion while musicians, attendants and guests fill the terraces and garden. The quiet embrace at the center makes the surrounding celebration feel even more alive.
notes: deep indigo, shadows in the illuminated heading
royal violet, the floral panels and bed textiles
pavilion blue, the broad wall behind the couple
jade, the geometric tilework and clothing
garden green, trees and foliage around the guests
soft gold, the chamber floor and yellow garments
parchment, the page and pale architectural details
vermilion, robes and warm textile accents
crimson, the bedcover and flowering details
